content.content:
title:	Реконструкция данных на историческую дату (стенд для проверки методики)
state:	OPEN
author:	investzhadrayev-creator
labels:	
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	
milestone:	
issue-type:	
parent:	
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	
blocking:	
number:	14
--
@claude Нужен стенд, позволяющий собрать входные данные оценки на произвольную дату в прошлом, без заглядывания в будущее. Это подготовка к проверке методики на исторических данных; сама проверка задачей не ставится.

Работать только в новейшем каталоге CONSILIUM_REPO_v4_2_*. Файл воркфлоу n8n не трогать — он вне твоих возможностей, это измерено.

Что сделать
1. Фильтр «на дату» в разборщике отчётности

В microservice/edgar_facts.py добавить необязательный параметр as_of (строка вида YYYY-MM-DD).

Когда он задан, при выборе фактов учитывать только те, у которых дата подачи не позже as_of. В ответе SEC у каждого факта есть поле даты подачи — использовать его, а не дату окончания периода.

Смысл: получить ровно то, что было известно публике на тот день. Отсекаются и позднейшие уточнения отчётности, и данные, ещё не опубликованные.

Когда параметр не задан — поведение не меняется ни на йоту.

2. Параметр конечной даты в запросе цен

В microservice/macro_prices.py уже используется адрес https://api.tiingo.com/tiingo/daily/{ticker}/prices с параметром startDate (строка 91). Ключ читается из окружения как TIINGO_TOKEN.

Сделать функцию, которая по тикеру и дате возвращает цену закрытия того дня — используя тот же адрес с startDate и endDate, равными искомой дате.

Из ответа вернуть все поля, относящиеся к цене и корпоративным действиям, включая нескорректированную цену, скорректированную и коэффициент сплита. Ничего не отбрасывать: точный состав полей нужен для следующего пункта, и он должен быть виден в результате, а не угадан.

3. Приведение цены и прибыли к одной базе акций — главное

Это самое важное в задаче.

Скорректированная цена выражена в сегодняшней базе акций. Прибыль на акцию из отчёта, поданного в прошлом, выражена в базе того времени. Если их перемножить как есть, отношение цены к прибыли будет ошибочным ровно в кратность сплита — например, при сплите десять к одному оно окажется заниженным в десять раз.

Сделать так, чтобы цена и прибыль всегда оказывались в одной базе. Какую базу выбрать — на твоё усмотрение, но выбор должен быть объяснён в комментарии.

Отсутствие данных для приведения — отказ, а не подстановка коэффициента 1. Здесь молчаливая единица опаснее ошибки: результат будет выглядеть правдоподобно и уверенно.

4. Собственный капитал и доходность капитала — новый вход, его сейчас нет вовсе

Проверено: в выдаче edgar_facts.py нет ни собственного капитала, ни доходности капитала. А новое правило терминального множителя (см. mailbox/PREREG_2026-08-06_HISTORICAL_VALIDATION.md, §8) требует медиану ROE за пять лет. Без этого поля стенд не запустится.

Сделать в edgar_facts.py:

собрать годовой ряд собственного капитала из отчётности (базовый тег StockholdersEquity; если он пуст — комбинированный StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest, с флагом, что взята комбинированная величина);
посчитать ROE по годам как прибыль за год к капиталу на конец года и выдать медиану за последние пять лет, поле roe_median_5y;
фильтр «на дату» из пункта 1 применяется и здесь: при заданном as_of в ряд попадают только значения, поданные к тому дню;
отрицательный или нулевой капитал — отказ по полю с причиной (roe_not_computable: negative_equity), не ноль и не пропуск молча. Компании с отрицательным капиталом от выкупов существуют, и для них ROE как вход формулы не определён;
меньше трёх годовых точек — тоже отказ по полю, с причиной insufficient_history.
5. Пины

Обязательны, иначе работа не принимается:

при заданной дате не попадает ни один факт, поданный позже неё;
при незаданной дате результат совпадает с нынешним поведением;
отношение цены к прибыли для тикера со сплитом после проверяемой даты совпадает с посчитанным вручную — этот пин главный;
при невозможности определить коэффициент сплита возвращается отказ, а не результат;
при отрицательном капитале поле ROE содержит отказ с причиной, а не число;
при заданной дате в ряд капитала не попадает ни одно значение, поданное позже неё.

Каждый пин проверяет свойство, а не форму: не имя переменной и не порядок строк, а то, что охраняется.

6. Мутации

В tools/mutation_probe.py добавить кейсы, доказывающие, что пины из пункта 4 умеют краснеть. Как минимум: снятие фильтра по дате обязано покраснеть; замена коэффициента сплита на единицу обязана покраснеть.

Учти: дефект маршрутизации каталога (js-селекторы уходили в питоновский запускатель) починен в v4.2.83 — работай от новейшего дерева. Добавляй кейсы так, чтобы селектор указывал на конкретный тестовый метод.

Чего не делать
Не трогать microservice/ivc_lib.py — там пинованная арифметика.
Не менять поведение при незаданной дате.
Не реализовывать саму историческую проверку, не заводить прогоны по списку имён.
Не трогать .github/workflows/.
Перед отгрузкой

Выполнить в каталоге версии и привести вывод в описании заявки:

npm install
python run_tests.py
python tools/mutation_probe.py

Создать ветку, открыть заявку. В основную ветку не писать. В описании заявки подтвердить, что при незаданной дате числа до и после правки совпадают.

content.content:
1	# Consilium Spine — AI-assisted equity research pipeline
2	
3	This repo runs real money decisions. Read this file before changing anything.
4	
5	## What this is
6	
7	An n8n workflow + a Flask microservice that produce an investment-committee memo for a ticker.
8	The mandate is 12–16% CAGR over 10 years with a **12% hurdle floor** and Graham-Dodd margin-of-
9	safety discipline. The output is a verdict (BUY / WATCH+ / NEUTRAL / AVOID) with an auditable
10	numeric trail.
11	
12	Two paths:
13	- **Core-P** — profitable companies. IVC/DCF-style valuation, GPS scorecard, gates, audit, arbiter.
14	- **Core-V** — pre-profit / Category-F names. Scenario tree, survival analysis, venture discount.
15	
16	## The one idea that matters
17	
18	> **LLM does judgment. Python does math.**
19	
20	Every field an LLM could write freely eventually smuggled in a defect. The fix was never a
21	better prompt — it was always **moving the logic into the deterministic layer**. The history:
22	
23	- LLM wrote the wiring code → it flaked, double-counted GPS blocks, sometimes crashed →
24	  replaced by a fixed harness (`analyze()`), and Stage2a now emits a JSON *spec*, not code.
25	- LLM declared the GPS total → it disagreed with the visible blocks → total is now the sum,
26	  by construction.
27	- LLM justified `future_pe` → it overreached → the cap is now enforced deterministically.
28	- LLM cited insider trades from prose → it produced a $2.76/share trade on a $1,852 stock →
29	  now read from SEC Form 4 XML, with grants/vesting structurally separated from real buys.
30	- The harness collapsed the mandate's THREE verdict bands into two → **BUY was structurally
31	  unreachable for every name, forever** → three bands restored (<12 AVOID / 12-16 WATCH+ /
32	  >=16 BUY), with a test that pins BUY reachability. The operator noticed this before the
33	  tests did.
34	- GAAP EPS double-counts SBC (charged in earnings AND diluting the count) → every SBC-heavy
35	  software name was structurally AVOID → dual basis: both legs priced, verdict follows the
36	  conservative one, and a >40% gap forces the memo to argue which basis is right.
37	- Diagnostics fired on artifacts: a fear-discount flag from comparing trailing-3y vs
38	  trailing-5y growth (overlapping windows), and a 568% incremental ROIC from dividing by an
39	  asset-light capex base. Both appeared in the run that produced the first-ever BUY — the
40	  worst possible moment for a phantom confirmation. Now: no forward estimate → no divergence
41	  claim at all; capex <5% of revenue → `not_meaningful`.
42	- `PEER_MAP` was a stub covering 8 tickers, so the entire portfolio silently got `peers=[]`.
43	  It looked exactly like a Yahoo outage. Not every data gap is an outage — check coverage
44	  before blaming the source.
45	
46	If you find yourself writing a prompt to *ask* a model to be accurate about a number, stop.
47	Move it to Python instead.
48	
49	## Source hierarchy
50	
51	Prefer the ORIGIN of a number over anyone who republishes it, and compute ratios rather than
52	ingesting ready-made ones:
53	
54	1. **SEC EDGAR** — all historical financials, share counts, insider Form 4. Never breaks.
55	2. **FINRA** — short interest. They collect it; Yahoo and every aggregator resell it.
56	3. **Alpha Vantage / Finnhub / Tiingo** — forward consensus, revision trends, prices.
57	4. **In-house computed** — peer P/E (EDGAR EPS x Tiingo price), fwd P/E (price / consensus EPS),
58	   short % (FINRA shares / EDGAR shares). Our arithmetic, auditable.
59	5. **yfinance** — last resort and cross-check only. Nulls out on cloud IPs without warning, and
60	   for a long time it was the ONLY source for every forward field. That was the bug.
61	
62	Two rules that follow:
63	
64	- **Divergence is loud.** Two sources disagreeing by >5% lands in `_divergence` — surfaced to
65	  the auditor, never silently averaged.
66	- **A number's BASIS travels with it.** Trailing P/E is not forward P/E. Shares outstanding is
67	  not float. FCF/share is not GAAP EPS. Every one of these pairs has already produced a wrong
68	  conclusion from a correct number in this pipeline. Label, or don't report.
69	
70	## Layout
71	
72	```
73	microservice/     Flask service (deployed to Railway as "growth-enrich"). ONE service, 9 routes.
74	  app.py            /health /enrich_yf /scenario_tree /edgar_facts /edgar_form4
75	                    /market_facts /macro_prices /analyze /cost
76	  pricing.py        v4.2.5. ONE home for LLM rates. Tokens are facts (provider usage blocks);
77	                    dollars are an ESTIMATE carrying the table's date. An unpriced model is
78	                    [UNVERIFIED], never $0 -- a run is never free. See SETUP_billing.md.
79	                    (this list said "7 routes" and omitted /macro_prices until 2026-07-17.
80	                     Not cosmetic: /macro_prices supplies pe_hist_median, the PE cap's best
81	                     anchor, and is smoke check #1 in VERIFY.md.)
82	                    `analyze()` IS the deterministic harness. This is the money-critical function.
83	  ivc_lib.py        PINNED valuation math (ivc, bull_bear_table, gps_quant). Treat as frozen.
84	  edgar_facts.py    SEC XBRL financials + sanity gates + confirmed-split detection.
85	  edgar_form4.py    SEC Form 4 insider transactions (discretionary P/S vs grants/vesting).
86	  market_facts.py   Second-source market layer: Alpha Vantage consensus, Finnhub revision
87	                    trends, in-house peer P/E (EDGAR EPS x Tiingo price), FINRA short interest,
88	                    and a >5% quorum check between sources.
89	  finra_short_interest.py  FINRA consolidatedShortInterest (OAuth2 client-credentials).
90	  scenario_f.py     Core-V Category-F scenario anchors.
91	  enrich_yf.py      yfinance enrichment (peers, PEG, ERB). Best-effort tier, degrades to null.
92	workflow/         The n8n workflow JSON. Highest version number = current.
93	tests/            Offline regression suite. Every test encodes a bug that actually happened.
94	```
95	
96	There is no `/run` route and no code execution anywhere. That was removed deliberately —
97	after the harness landed, nothing needed to execute LLM-written code, so the capability was
98	deleted rather than left lying around.
99	
100	## Commands
101	
102	```bash
103	npm install                                 # ONCE per container. eslint 8, for the undef gate.
104	                                            # Skip it and run_tests.py prints NOT VERIFIED.
105	python3 run_tests.py                        # whole suite: offline, free, <1s. Do this before every deploy.
106	python3 -m unittest discover tests          # python tests only
107	node tests/test_render_tables.js            # the JS nodes (Render Tables / Build Radar)
108	
109	cd microservice && python3 edgar_facts.py --selftest    # offline
110	cd microservice && python3 edgar_form4.py --selftest     # offline
111	cd microservice && python3 edgar_form4.py NOW            # LIVE SEC call — use sparingly, respect rate limits
112	cd microservice && python3 finra_short_interest.py AAPL <client_id> <client_secret>   # LIVE FINRA call
113	```
114	
115	`requirements.txt` pins the deployed set. The python suite needs only `flask` — yfinance and
116	curl_cffi are imported lazily inside functions and are never touched by tests. The JS gates need
117	`node` plus `eslint` 8 (`package.json`, dev-only, never deployed). Absent either, the runner
118	reports NOT VERIFIED rather than green: for a long time it reported green instead, which is why
119	`package.json` exists at all.
120	
121	## Rules
122	
123	**Never weaken a gate to make a ticker pass.**
124	A BLOCKING gate that fires is the system working. If a healthy name is being rejected, the bug
125	is upstream in the deterministic layer — fix it there. Loosening a threshold, widening a
126	tolerance, or downgrading BLOCKING→MAJOR to get a green run destroys the margin of safety this
127	whole system exists to enforce, and it does so *silently*: the tests still pass and the report
128	still looks authoritative. This is the single most damaging change you could make here.
129	The three gates that were correctly relaxed (GPS_TOTAL_MISMATCH, gate_override,
130	pe_cap_unjustified) were relaxed **only after** the deterministic layer made the check
131	structurally unnecessary — never to make a run go green.
132	
133	**Ask before touching these.** They are load-bearing for correctness, not style:
134	- `microservice/ivc_lib.py` — pinned valuation math
135	- `analyze()` in `microservice/app.py` — the harness
136	- gate/threshold logic in any prompt (`stage4`, `stage5_auditor`, `core_v_auditor`)
137	- `hurdle` (0.12), the PE-CAP constants, the venture discount rate
138	
139	**Run the tests before proposing any diff to microservice/ or workflow/.** If a change is
140	money-critical, show the before/after numbers on a concrete ticker profile, not just "tests
141	pass".
142	
143	**Never touch the n8n service's own env vars.** All data-source keys belong to the
144	growth-enrich service. Railway's RAW Editor REPLACES the variable set rather than appending to
145	it, and the n8n service's set includes `N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY` — wipe it and every stored
146	credential becomes undecryptable ("a different encryptionKey was used"). Workflows survive
147	(they aren't encrypted); credentials must be recreated. This already happened once, following
148	setup instructions that were themselves wrong — the instruction, not the operator, was the
149	defect.
150	
151	**Change the topology → bump the meter map.** `Collect Usage` holds a second copy of the path
152	topology (the `NOT_ON_PATH` set: disabled Grok, the Core-V branch, and — under gated mode — Stage
153	5/6). It decides whether a stage's silence is a free zero (`not_run`) or spent-but-unmeasured money
154	(`meter_lost`). If you re-wire a stage (re-enable Grok, add an LLM node, re-route Core-V) and leave
155	that set stale, the meters lie again — silently, the way they did on 2026-07-18. So: any edit to the
156	workflow connections that adds, removes, or re-routes an LLM stage MUST update `NOT_ON_PATH` in the
157	same changeset. `TestMeterMapTopologyV4221` pins the map to the actual graph and fails on drift
158	(negative-control verified: re-wiring Grok without touching the map turns it red).
159	
160	**ALL GREEN means the runner's exit code is 0 — and you say so explicitly in the handoff.** Not "the
161	python summary printed OK", not a grep of the log. `python run_tests.py; echo $?` must print `0`, and
162	the handoff must name it. A partial grep once masked a JS gate that had been red since v4.2.20
163	(`test_cost_section.js`), and "safe to deploy" was claimed on a run whose true exit code was 1. A
164	check whose result you did not read has not passed.
165	
166	**Diagnose an integration defect from the source's RAW response, never from the symptom in the
167	report.** A null/`[UNVERIFIED]` field in the output tells you *that* something failed, not *why* or
168	*where*. The 2026-07-19 case: `fwd_pe` printed `[UNVERIFIED]`, the backlog blamed the AV key, and the
169	operator swapped the AV key three times to no effect — because `fwd_pe` reaches the report from Yahoo
170	(rate-limited on cloud IPs), and AV's own `forward_pe_reported` was locked behind an `eps_ttm`/growth
171	gate it never cleared. Only reading the actual `/market_facts` response path found it. So: before
172	proposing a cause, trace the field back through the raw response of each source it touches; a fix aimed
173	at the symptom's assumed cause is a guess until the raw log confirms it.
174	
175	**Never edit node source by position.** Two v4.2 defects, one root cause. (1) A patch spliced
176	`Gather Data` by character offset and chopped 87 chars off its head -> `SyntaxError: Unexpected
177	token ')'` in production; the workflow JSON stayed valid and every python test passed, because
178	nothing in the suite parsed node source. (2) v4.0 packs three consts onto ONE line
179	(`const FINN=...; const TIINGO=...; const AVKEY=...;`), so a line-oriented regex intended for a
180	later comment matched the FIRST `//` on a merged line and ate a freshly-inserted comment.
181	Both are the same mistake: treating JS source as positions/lines rather than as anchored text.
182	Rules: anchor on exact substrings; when a region spans several statements, replace the WHOLE
183	span in one cut; re-parse every touched node afterwards (`node tests/test_syntax.js`, now in
184	run_tests.py, 18 nodes, negative-control verified).
185	
186	**One canonical home per fact.** Env-var NAMES live in SETUP_railway.md, nowhere else -- not in
187	JS comments, not in the changelog. The secret-hygiene test scans for the bare names, and a
188	comment reciting them trips it. That is the test being right for a slightly wrong reason, but
189	the fix is still to reword rather than exempt comments: a stale name in an old changelog entry
190	is something a reader can copy back into the JSON, reopening exactly the leak v4.2 closed.
191	
192	**A green suite is not coverage.** Every render block sits behind `if (isObj(res.<section>))`.
193	If the mock in `tests/test_render_tables.js` lacks that key, the branch never executes and the
194	test passes without testing anything — that is exactly how a `gt is not defined` ReferenceError
195	reached a live run while the suite reported 10/10. **Adding a render section requires extending
196	MOCK_RESULT in the same change.** When you fix a bug the suite missed, ask first why it missed
197	it, and fix that too.
198	
199	The same disease reached the RUNNER (found 2026-07-17). `test_undef.js` exited **0** when eslint
200	was missing, so `run_tests.py` printed "ALL GREEN — safe to deploy" having resolved zero
201	identifiers in zero nodes — and eslint is missing in every fresh container, which is every chat
202	session. The gate that exists because `gt is not defined` shipped twice was itself the gate not
203	running, and the only trace was one dim stderr line that any `| tail` swallowed. Both JS gates
204	now enforce a coverage floor (`total >= 19`), missing tooling exits **2**, and the runner prints
205	**NOT VERIFIED** — a third state, distinct from pass and fail, because "did not run" is neither.
206	The rule generalises: **a check reports what it examined, or it reports nothing. Never let
207	"skipped" and "passed" print the same word.** This is the v4.2.2 lesson — unknown spelled "0" —
208	one level up, in the very thing that certifies the others.
209	
210	And a third face of it, found 2026-07-17 by reading a live report rather than by any test: an
211	honest number computed and then DISCARDED AT THE BOUNDARY. `gps_quant` correctly reduced a
212	block's max and correctly asked for `implied_cagr_base`; `analyze()` hardcoded the nominal maxima
213	over the first and never supplied the second. Both units were individually correct and 165 tests
214	passed, because every test drove `gps_quant` and none drove its CALLER. **Where a docstring says
215	"consumers must read X", write the test against the CONSUMER.** A contract asserted only in prose
216	is a contract nobody checks — and the caller is where contracts die.
217	
218	**Honest failure beats an invented number.** If a driver is missing, return an error and let
219	the run fail conservatively. Never substitute a plausible default for a number you don't have.
220	`growth_rate` and `future_pe` are deliberately None-able for exactly this reason.
221	
222	**Missing data is null, never zero.** A zero flows through arithmetic and corrupts everything
223	downstream; a null stops and says so. Placeholder zeros from EDGAR are dropped and *recorded*
224	in `_flags.dropped_zero` — visible, not silent.
225	
226	**Don't trust the LLM spec's shape.** `dict.get(k, default)` does NOT substitute the default
227	when the key exists with value `None` — that exact gotcha emptied PLTR's entire numeric layer.
228	Sanitize at the boundary.
229	
230	**Never run with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in this repo.** It's a financial tool; a
231	silently auto-approved bad edit costs real money.
232	
233	## Language
234	
235	The report is written in **English** (it's fed to NotebookLM, which translates to Russian and
236	preserves the numbers). Deterministic nodes that render report text — `Render Tables`,
237	`Build Radar`, `Assemble Report`, `Assemble Core-V` — must contain **zero Cyrillic**; there is
238	a test for this, because the leak happened twice.
239	
240	Two deliberate exceptions:
241	- `Prompts Growth` — Russian text there is *instructions* to a multilingual model, not output.
242	- `Gather Data` — its Russian strings are operator-facing Telegram errors shown to the user
243	  directly ("Пустой ввод — укажите тикер"). Correctly Russian. Leave them.
244	
245	## Deploy
246	
247	1. `python3 run_tests.py` — must be green.
248	2. Push `microservice/` to the growth-enrich Railway repo. Redeploy.
249	3. Import `workflow/consilium_spine_vX_Y.json` into n8n.
250	4. Nothing to fill in. As of v4.1 the workflow contains **no keys and no placeholders**: HTTP
251	   nodes bind to n8n credentials BY NAME (`Anthropic API`, `OpenAI API`, `xAI API`,
252	   `Perplexity API`, `Gemini API` — the last is Query Auth, the rest Header Auth), and code
253	   nodes read `$env.*` (`PYTHON_SERVICE_URL`, `TIINGO_TOKEN`, `FRED_KEY`, `FINNHUB_KEY`,
254	   `ALPHAVANTAGE_KEY`, `FINRA_CLIENT_ID`, `FINRA_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SEC_USER_AGENT`,
255	   `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`). Credential names must match exactly or n8n won't rebind on import.
256	   **Never reintroduce a key into the JSON** — the export is meant to be safe to share, and
257	   that property is only one careless edit away from being lost.
258	5. Set the env vars (docker-compose) and create the credentials — once, see SETUP.md §3.3.
259	   A missing key disables only its own source: the run degrades to `[UNVERIFIED]` rather than
260	   failing. FINRA credential type must be **Public**, not Mock (Mock returns randomized data).
261	6. `SEC_USER_AGENT` must carry a real contact email (SEC fair-access rule). It is an **env var
262	   on growth-enrich** — `edgar_facts.py` reads it via `os.environ.get` and falls back to a
263	   string containing `SEC_USER_AGENT NOT SET`, which is what to grep the Railway logs for. This
264	   said "the constant in `edgar_facts.py` for the Railway side" until 2026-07-17; that was
265	   stale, and SETUP.md §1.2 still told the operator to hardcode it. Do not edit the source.
266	7. Set `Consilium Error Handler` as the workflow's Error workflow, or failures stay silent
267	   until someone opens n8n.
268	
269	## Known open items
270	
271	- **PE-CAP no-anchor default (20x)** is a blunt constant. If live runs show it systematically
272	  mis-pricing a sector, make it sector-aware — but only with evidence from real runs.
273	- **Form4 lookback** is capped at 40 filings / 270 days. A mega-cap with very active insiders
274	  could brush the node's 40s timeout.
275	- **Render Tables is ~26KB** of rendering logic. The Cyrillic tests cover the paths a normal
276	  run takes; a rare branch could still hide something.
277	- **Verdicts are unstable at band edges.** ADBE landed BUY at 16.22% implied CAGR against a
278	  16.0% threshold — a 0.22pp margin, while `growth_rate`/`future_pe` are LLM judgment that
279	  drifts between runs (a prior run gave 18.08% and WATCH+). Any threshold has an edge; just
280	  don't read a near-edge verdict as precision.
281	- **The hurdle (12%) sits below the operator's own goal** (~15-18% CAGR to reach the target).
282	  Approving 12-13% names cannot compound to the goal. Unresolved by design — the operator
283	  decides whether to raise the hurdle or make up the gap in the speculative sleeve.
284	- **Owner-earnings third leg.** The FCF leg punishes capex-heavy names (MSFT), which is the
285	  market's fear materialized rather than an accounting artifact. A maintenance-capex-only
286	  ("owner earnings") leg would address it, but splitting growth vs maintenance capex is
287	  judgment, not a fact — needs the operator's call before building.
288	- **No last-known-good cache.** A transient source outage still nulls a field for that run.
289	  Approved in principle, not built.
290	
291	## Lesson (v4.2.2, NFLX 2026-07-16): "unknown" needs a vocabulary, or it gets spelled "0"
292	
293	Four defects in one run. All four came from the **deterministic layer** — the one we call
294	trusted. All four were caught by an **LLM**: Stage 2b read `growth_diag` and wrote that the EPS
295	CAGR was "contaminated"; Stage 2b named the trailing peer multiple as WBD's distressed 95x;
296	Stage 2b diagnosed the C block as "structurally starved of forward-PE data, not a judgment that
297	valuation is cheap." The judgment layer worked exactly as designed. The math layer lied.
298	
299	"LLM does judgment, Python does math" remains right. It does **not** follow that Python is
300	therefore correct. Our tests checked that code parses, that identifiers resolve, that secrets do
301	not leak. Not one checked that a **number means what it says**.
302	
303	The root pattern, `0 if x is None else ...`, appeared nine times. It reads as conservative and
304	is the opposite: it states a confident falsehood where it should state a gap. NFLX paid three
305	ways at once — punished for a split we failed to confirm, punished for dilution while it was
306	buying back 96.5% of FCF, punished for a valuation field we never fetched. A reader cannot
307	distinguish "scored zero" from "we didn't look", and neither can the memo, the auditor or the
308	arbiter downstream. **A model with no way to say "I don't know" will say something else instead,
309	and it will sound just as certain.**
310	
311	Corollaries earned here, each with a case of record:
312	
313	- **The basis travels with the number, or the number is a lie.** A 2022 numerator over a 2026
314	  denominator; a trailing median under a hardcoded "fwd" label. Both survived every gate because
315	  gates check *values*, and the defect was in the *units*.
316	- **A client-side sort cannot repair a server-side truncation.** We sorted the wrong 60 rows for
317	  three and a half years.
318	- **A wrong anchor is worse than no anchor.** A 143x PE cap is not a loose cap; it is the
319	  absence of one, wearing a cap's name.
320	- **Absence must be stated.** `confirmed_splits` returning empty was indistinguishable from
321	  "no split ever happened" — so a real split became 56%/yr dilution.
322	- **What the reader never sees reaches the verdict anyway.** Hence the DATA DEFECTS banner.
323	
324	Note what held: the verdict. `eps0` is a single year and never spanned the break, so IV, PWFV,
325	MoS and implied_cagr were clean and AVOID was correct throughout. The defects hit *comparisons
326	across time*, not point-in-time facts. That distinction is the reason to keep the deterministic
327	and judgment layers separate — and the reason to stop assuming the deterministic one is honest
328	just because it is code.
329	
330	## Работа с workflow/ — контекстная бомба
331	Поля jsCode в спайне — одиночные строки до 58 000 символов. Обычный grep по workflow/*.json
332	выбрасывает в контекст сотни килобайт и съедает треть окна чата. ВСЕГДА используй grep -c или
333	grep -o с узким шаблоном, либо читай через python3 с точечным срезом по индексу. Никогда не
334	печатай ноду целиком. В репозитории держится ТОЛЬКО текущий спайн — мёртвые версии удаляются при
335	бампе, их история остаётся в HANDOFF.
336

# Consilium Spine — AI-assisted equity research pipeline

This repo runs real money decisions. Read this file before changing anything.

## What this is

An n8n workflow + a Flask microservice that produce an investment-committee memo for a ticker.
The mandate is 12–16% CAGR over 10 years with a **12% hurdle floor** and Graham-Dodd margin-of-
safety discipline. The output is a verdict (BUY / WATCH+ / NEUTRAL / AVOID) with an auditable
numeric trail.

Two paths:
- **Core-P** — profitable companies. IVC/DCF-style valuation, GPS scorecard, gates, audit, arbiter.
- **Core-V** — pre-profit / Category-F names. Scenario tree, survival analysis, venture discount.

## The one idea that matters

> **LLM does judgment. Python does math.**

Every field an LLM could write freely eventually smuggled in a defect. The fix was never a
better prompt — it was always **moving the logic into the deterministic layer**. The history:

- LLM wrote the wiring code → it flaked, double-counted GPS blocks, sometimes crashed →
  replaced by a fixed harness (`analyze()`), and Stage2a now emits a JSON *spec*, not code.
- LLM declared the GPS total → it disagreed with the visible blocks → total is now the sum,
  by construction.
- LLM justified `future_pe` → it overreached → the cap is now enforced deterministically.
- LLM cited insider trades from prose → it produced a $2.76/share trade on a $1,852 stock →
  now read from SEC Form 4 XML, with grants/vesting structurally separated from real buys.
- The harness collapsed the mandate's THREE verdict bands into two → **BUY was structurally
  unreachable for every name, forever** → three bands restored (<12 AVOID / 12-16 WATCH+ /
  >=16 BUY), with a test that pins BUY reachability. The operator noticed this before the
  tests did.
- GAAP EPS double-counts SBC (charged in earnings AND diluting the count) → every SBC-heavy
  software name was structurally AVOID → dual basis: both legs priced, verdict follows the
  conservative one, and a >40% gap forces the memo to argue which basis is right.
- Diagnostics fired on artifacts: a fear-discount flag from comparing trailing-3y vs
  trailing-5y growth (overlapping windows), and a 568% incremental ROIC from dividing by an
  asset-light capex base. Both appeared in the run that produced the first-ever BUY — the
  worst possible moment for a phantom confirmation. Now: no forward estimate → no divergence
  claim at all; capex <5% of revenue → `not_meaningful`.
- `PEER_MAP` was a stub covering 8 tickers, so the entire portfolio silently got `peers=[]`.
  It looked exactly like a Yahoo outage. Not every data gap is an outage — check coverage
  before blaming the source.

If you find yourself writing a prompt to *ask* a model to be accurate about a number, stop.
Move it to Python instead.

## Source hierarchy

Prefer the ORIGIN of a number over anyone who republishes it, and compute ratios rather than
ingesting ready-made ones:

1. **SEC EDGAR** — all historical financials, share counts, insider Form 4. Never breaks.
2. **FINRA** — short interest. They collect it; Yahoo and every aggregator resell it.
3. **Alpha Vantage / Finnhub / Tiingo** — forward consensus, revision trends, prices.
4. **In-house computed** — peer P/E (EDGAR EPS x Tiingo price), fwd P/E (price / consensus EPS),
   short % (FINRA shares / EDGAR shares). Our arithmetic, auditable.
5. **yfinance** — last resort and cross-check only. Nulls out on cloud IPs without warning, and
   for a long time it was the ONLY source for every forward field. That was the bug.

Two rules that follow:

- **Divergence is loud.** Two sources disagreeing by >5% lands in `_divergence` — surfaced to
  the auditor, never silently averaged.
- **A number's BASIS travels with it.** Trailing P/E is not forward P/E. Shares outstanding is
  not float. FCF/share is not GAAP EPS. Every one of these pairs has already produced a wrong
  conclusion from a correct number in this pipeline. Label, or don't report.

## Layout

```
microservice/     Flask service (deployed to Railway as "growth-enrich"). ONE service, 9 routes.
  app.py            /health /enrich_yf /scenario_tree /edgar_facts /edgar_form4
                    /market_facts /macro_prices /analyze /cost
  pricing.py        v4.2.5. ONE home for LLM rates. Tokens are facts (provider usage blocks);
                    dollars are an ESTIMATE carrying the table's date. An unpriced model is
                    [UNVERIFIED], never $0 -- a run is never free. See SETUP_billing.md.
                    (this list said "7 routes" and omitted /macro_prices until 2026-07-17.
                     Not cosmetic: /macro_prices supplies pe_hist_median, the PE cap's best
                     anchor, and is smoke check #1 in VERIFY.md.)
                    `analyze()` IS the deterministic harness. This is the money-critical function.
  ivc_lib.py        PINNED valuation math (ivc, bull_bear_table, gps_quant). Treat as frozen.
  edgar_facts.py    SEC XBRL financials + sanity gates + confirmed-split detection.
  edgar_form4.py    SEC Form 4 insider transactions (discretionary P/S vs grants/vesting).
  market_facts.py   Second-source market layer: Alpha Vantage consensus, Finnhub revision
                    trends, in-house peer P/E (EDGAR EPS x Tiingo price), FINRA short interest,
                    and a >5% quorum check between sources.
  finra_short_interest.py  FINRA consolidatedShortInterest (OAuth2 client-credentials).
  scenario_f.py     Core-V Category-F scenario anchors.
  enrich_yf.py      yfinance enrichment (peers, PEG, ERB). Best-effort tier, degrades to null.
workflow/         The n8n workflow JSON. Highest version number = current.
tests/            Offline regression suite. Every test encodes a bug that actually happened.
```

There is no `/run` route and no code execution anywhere. That was removed deliberately —
after the harness landed, nothing needed to execute LLM-written code, so the capability was
deleted rather than left lying around.

## Commands

```bash
npm install                                 # ONCE per container. eslint 8, for the undef gate.
                                            # Skip it and run_tests.py prints NOT VERIFIED.
python3 run_tests.py                        # whole suite: offline, free, <1s. Do this before every deploy.
python3 -m unittest discover tests          # python tests only
node tests/test_render_tables.js            # the JS nodes (Render Tables / Build Radar)

cd microservice && python3 edgar_facts.py --selftest    # offline
cd microservice && python3 edgar_form4.py --selftest     # offline
cd microservice && python3 edgar_form4.py NOW            # LIVE SEC call — use sparingly, respect rate limits
cd microservice && python3 finra_short_interest.py AAPL <client_id> <client_secret>   # LIVE FINRA call
```

`requirements.txt` pins the deployed set. The python suite needs only `flask` — yfinance and
curl_cffi are imported lazily inside functions and are never touched by tests. The JS gates need
`node` plus `eslint` 8 (`package.json`, dev-only, never deployed). Absent either, the runner
reports NOT VERIFIED rather than green: for a long time it reported green instead, which is why
`package.json` exists at all.

## Rules

**Never weaken a gate to make a ticker pass.**
A BLOCKING gate that fires is the system working. If a healthy name is being rejected, the bug
is upstream in the deterministic layer — fix it there. Loosening a threshold, widening a
tolerance, or downgrading BLOCKING→MAJOR to get a green run destroys the margin of safety this
whole system exists to enforce, and it does so *silently*: the tests still pass and the report
still looks authoritative. This is the single most damaging change you could make here.
The three gates that were correctly relaxed (GPS_TOTAL_MISMATCH, gate_override,
pe_cap_unjustified) were relaxed **only after** the deterministic layer made the check
structurally unnecessary — never to make a run go green.

**Ask before touching these.** They are load-bearing for correctness, not style:
- `microservice/ivc_lib.py` — pinned valuation math
- `analyze()` in `microservice/app.py` — the harness
- gate/threshold logic in any prompt (`stage4`, `stage5_auditor`, `core_v_auditor`)
- `hurdle` (0.12), the PE-CAP constants, the venture discount rate

**Run the tests before proposing any diff to microservice/ or workflow/.** If a change is
money-critical, show the before/after numbers on a concrete ticker profile, not just "tests
pass".

**Never touch the n8n service's own env vars.** All data-source keys belong to the
growth-enrich service. Railway's RAW Editor REPLACES the variable set rather than appending to
it, and the n8n service's set includes `N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY` — wipe it and every stored
credential becomes undecryptable ("a different encryptionKey was used"). Workflows survive
(they aren't encrypted); credentials must be recreated. This already happened once, following
setup instructions that were themselves wrong — the instruction, not the operator, was the
defect.

**Change the topology → bump the meter map.** `Collect Usage` holds a second copy of the path
topology (the `NOT_ON_PATH` set: disabled Grok, the Core-V branch, and — under gated mode — Stage
5/6). It decides whether a stage's silence is a free zero (`not_run`) or spent-but-unmeasured money
(`meter_lost`). If you re-wire a stage (re-enable Grok, add an LLM node, re-route Core-V) and leave
that set stale, the meters lie again — silently, the way they did on 2026-07-18. So: any edit to the
workflow connections that adds, removes, or re-routes an LLM stage MUST update `NOT_ON_PATH` in the
same changeset. `TestMeterMapTopologyV4221` pins the map to the actual graph and fails on drift
(negative-control verified: re-wiring Grok without touching the map turns it red).

**ALL GREEN means the runner's exit code is 0 — and you say so explicitly in the handoff.** Not "the
python summary printed OK", not a grep of the log. `python run_tests.py; echo $?` must print `0`, and
the handoff must name it. A partial grep once masked a JS gate that had been red since v4.2.20
(`test_cost_section.js`), and "safe to deploy" was claimed on a run whose true exit code was 1. A
check whose result you did not read has not passed.

**Diagnose an integration defect from the source's RAW response, never from the symptom in the
report.** A null/`[UNVERIFIED]` field in the output tells you *that* something failed, not *why* or
*where*. The 2026-07-19 case: `fwd_pe` printed `[UNVERIFIED]`, the backlog blamed the AV key, and the
operator swapped the AV key three times to no effect — because `fwd_pe` reaches the report from Yahoo
(rate-limited on cloud IPs), and AV's own `forward_pe_reported` was locked behind an `eps_ttm`/growth
gate it never cleared. Only reading the actual `/market_facts` response path found it. So: before
proposing a cause, trace the field back through the raw response of each source it touches; a fix aimed
at the symptom's assumed cause is a guess until the raw log confirms it.

**Never edit node source by position.** Two v4.2 defects, one root cause. (1) A patch spliced
`Gather Data` by character offset and chopped 87 chars off its head -> `SyntaxError: Unexpected
token ')'` in production; the workflow JSON stayed valid and every python test passed, because
nothing in the suite parsed node source. (2) v4.0 packs three consts onto ONE line
(`const FINN=...; const TIINGO=...; const AVKEY=...;`), so a line-oriented regex intended for a
later comment matched the FIRST `//` on a merged line and ate a freshly-inserted comment.
Both are the same mistake: treating JS source as positions/lines rather than as anchored text.
Rules: anchor on exact substrings; when a region spans several statements, replace the WHOLE
span in one cut; re-parse every touched node afterwards (`node tests/test_syntax.js`, now in
run_tests.py, 18 nodes, negative-control verified).

**One canonical home per fact.** Env-var NAMES live in SETUP_railway.md, nowhere else -- not in
JS comments, not in the changelog. The secret-hygiene test scans for the bare names, and a
comment reciting them trips it. That is the test being right for a slightly wrong reason, but
the fix is still to reword rather than exempt comments: a stale name in an old changelog entry
is something a reader can copy back into the JSON, reopening exactly the leak v4.2 closed.

**A green suite is not coverage.** Every render block sits behind `if (isObj(res.<section>))`.
If the mock in `tests/test_render_tables.js` lacks that key, the branch never executes and the
test passes without testing anything — that is exactly how a `gt is not defined` ReferenceError
reached a live run while the suite reported 10/10. **Adding a render section requires extending
MOCK_RESULT in the same change.** When you fix a bug the suite missed, ask first why it missed
it, and fix that too.

The same disease reached the RUNNER (found 2026-07-17). `test_undef.js` exited **0** when eslint
was missing, so `run_tests.py` printed "ALL GREEN — safe to deploy" having resolved zero
identifiers in zero nodes — and eslint is missing in every fresh container, which is every chat
session. The gate that exists because `gt is not defined` shipped twice was itself the gate not
running, and the only trace was one dim stderr line that any `| tail` swallowed. Both JS gates
now enforce a coverage floor (`total >= 19`), missing tooling exits **2**, and the runner prints
**NOT VERIFIED** — a third state, distinct from pass and fail, because "did not run" is neither.
The rule generalises: **a check reports what it examined, or it reports nothing. Never let
"skipped" and "passed" print the same word.** This is the v4.2.2 lesson — unknown spelled "0" —
one level up, in the very thing that certifies the others.

And a third face of it, found 2026-07-17 by reading a live report rather than by any test: an
honest number computed and then DISCARDED AT THE BOUNDARY. `gps_quant` correctly reduced a
block's max and correctly asked for `implied_cagr_base`; `analyze()` hardcoded the nominal maxima
over the first and never supplied the second. Both units were individually correct and 165 tests
passed, because every test drove `gps_quant` and none drove its CALLER. **Where a docstring says
"consumers must read X", write the test against the CONSUMER.** A contract asserted only in prose
is a contract nobody checks — and the caller is where contracts die.

**Honest failure beats an invented number.** If a driver is missing, return an error and let
the run fail conservatively. Never substitute a plausible default for a number you don't have.
`growth_rate` and `future_pe` are deliberately None-able for exactly this reason.

**Missing data is null, never zero.** A zero flows through arithmetic and corrupts everything
downstream; a null stops and says so. Placeholder zeros from EDGAR are dropped and *recorded*
in `_flags.dropped_zero` — visible, not silent.

**Don't trust the LLM spec's shape.** `dict.get(k, default)` does NOT substitute the default
when the key exists with value `None` — that exact gotcha emptied PLTR's entire numeric layer.
Sanitize at the boundary.

**Never run with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in this repo.** It's a financial tool; a
silently auto-approved bad edit costs real money.

## Language

The report is written in **English** (it's fed to NotebookLM, which translates to Russian and
preserves the numbers). Deterministic nodes that render report text — `Render Tables`,
`Build Radar`, `Assemble Report`, `Assemble Core-V` — must contain **zero Cyrillic**; there is
a test for this, because the leak happened twice.

Two deliberate exceptions:
- `Prompts Growth` — Russian text there is *instructions* to a multilingual model, not output.
- `Gather Data` — its Russian strings are operator-facing Telegram errors shown to the user
  directly ("Пустой ввод — укажите тикер"). Correctly Russian. Leave them.

## Deploy

1. `python3 run_tests.py` — must be green.
2. Push `microservice/` to the growth-enrich Railway repo. Redeploy.
3. Import `workflow/consilium_spine_vX_Y.json` into n8n.
4. Nothing to fill in. As of v4.1 the workflow contains **no keys and no placeholders**: HTTP
   nodes bind to n8n credentials BY NAME (`Anthropic API`, `OpenAI API`, `xAI API`,
   `Perplexity API`, `Gemini API` — the last is Query Auth, the rest Header Auth), and code
   nodes read `$env.*` (`PYTHON_SERVICE_URL`, `TIINGO_TOKEN`, `FRED_KEY`, `FINNHUB_KEY`,
   `ALPHAVANTAGE_KEY`, `FINRA_CLIENT_ID`, `FINRA_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SEC_USER_AGENT`,
   `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`). Credential names must match exactly or n8n won't rebind on import.
   **Never reintroduce a key into the JSON** — the export is meant to be safe to share, and
   that property is only one careless edit away from being lost.
5. Set the env vars (docker-compose) and create the credentials — once, see SETUP.md §3.3.
   A missing key disables only its own source: the run degrades to `[UNVERIFIED]` rather than
   failing. FINRA credential type must be **Public**, not Mock (Mock returns randomized data).
6. `SEC_USER_AGENT` must carry a real contact email (SEC fair-access rule). It is an **env var
   on growth-enrich** — `edgar_facts.py` reads it via `os.environ.get` and falls back to a
   string containing `SEC_USER_AGENT NOT SET`, which is what to grep the Railway logs for. This
   said "the constant in `edgar_facts.py` for the Railway side" until 2026-07-17; that was
   stale, and SETUP.md §1.2 still told the operator to hardcode it. Do not edit the source.
7. Set `Consilium Error Handler` as the workflow's Error workflow, or failures stay silent
   until someone opens n8n.

## Known open items

- **PE-CAP no-anchor default (20x)** is a blunt constant. If live runs show it systematically
  mis-pricing a sector, make it sector-aware — but only with evidence from real runs.
- **Form4 lookback** is capped at 40 filings / 270 days. A mega-cap with very active insiders
  could brush the node's 40s timeout.
- **Render Tables is ~26KB** of rendering logic. The Cyrillic tests cover the paths a normal
  run takes; a rare branch could still hide something.
- **Verdicts are unstable at band edges.** ADBE landed BUY at 16.22% implied CAGR against a
  16.0% threshold — a 0.22pp margin, while `growth_rate`/`future_pe` are LLM judgment that
  drifts between runs (a prior run gave 18.08% and WATCH+). Any threshold has an edge; just
  don't read a near-edge verdict as precision.
- **The hurdle (12%) sits below the operator's own goal** (~15-18% CAGR to reach the target).
  Approving 12-13% names cannot compound to the goal. Unresolved by design — the operator
  decides whether to raise the hurdle or make up the gap in the speculative sleeve.
- **Owner-earnings third leg.** The FCF leg punishes capex-heavy names (MSFT), which is the
  market's fear materialized rather than an accounting artifact. A maintenance-capex-only
  ("owner earnings") leg would address it, but splitting growth vs maintenance capex is
  judgment, not a fact — needs the operator's call before building.
- **No last-known-good cache.** A transient source outage still nulls a field for that run.
  Approved in principle, not built.

## Lesson (v4.2.2, NFLX 2026-07-16): "unknown" needs a vocabulary, or it gets spelled "0"

Four defects in one run. All four came from the **deterministic layer** — the one we call
trusted. All four were caught by an **LLM**: Stage 2b read `growth_diag` and wrote that the EPS
CAGR was "contaminated"; Stage 2b named the trailing peer multiple as WBD's distressed 95x;
Stage 2b diagnosed the C block as "structurally starved of forward-PE data, not a judgment that
valuation is cheap." The judgment layer worked exactly as designed. The math layer lied.

"LLM does judgment, Python does math" remains right. It does **not** follow that Python is
therefore correct. Our tests checked that code parses, that identifiers resolve, that secrets do
not leak. Not one checked that a **number means what it says**.

The root pattern, `0 if x is None else ...`, appeared nine times. It reads as conservative and
is the opposite: it states a confident falsehood where it should state a gap. NFLX paid three
ways at once — punished for a split we failed to confirm, punished for dilution while it was
buying back 96.5% of FCF, punished for a valuation field we never fetched. A reader cannot
distinguish "scored zero" from "we didn't look", and neither can the memo, the auditor or the
arbiter downstream. **A model with no way to say "I don't know" will say something else instead,
and it will sound just as certain.**

Corollaries earned here, each with a case of record:

- **The basis travels with the number, or the number is a lie.** A 2022 numerator over a 2026
  denominator; a trailing median under a hardcoded "fwd" label. Both survived every gate because
  gates check *values*, and the defect was in the *units*.
- **A client-side sort cannot repair a server-side truncation.** We sorted the wrong 60 rows for
  three and a half years.
- **A wrong anchor is worse than no anchor.** A 143x PE cap is not a loose cap; it is the
  absence of one, wearing a cap's name.
- **Absence must be stated.** `confirmed_splits` returning empty was indistinguishable from
  "no split ever happened" — so a real split became 56%/yr dilution.
- **What the reader never sees reaches the verdict anyway.** Hence the DATA DEFECTS banner.

Note what held: the verdict. `eps0` is a single year and never spanned the break, so IV, PWFV,
MoS and implied_cagr were clean and AVOID was correct throughout. The defects hit *comparisons
across time*, not point-in-time facts. That distinction is the reason to keep the deterministic
and judgment layers separate — and the reason to stop assuming the deterministic one is honest
just because it is code.

216	def _annual_merged(facts, tags, taxonomy="us-gaap", drop_zero=False):
217	    """Fill each fiscal-year-end with the highest-priority tag reporting it (gap-fill).
218	    Within a tag dedupe by end keeping latest 'filed'. drop_zero -> treat val==0 as absence.
219	    Returns (oldest-first [{end,val,accn,filed}], set(tags_used), [dropped_zero_ends])."""
220	    by_end, used, dropped = {}, set(), []
221	    # v4.2.45 (mandate BBB): collect EVERY tag's coverage FIRST, then prefer a SINGLE-TAG series.
222	    # The MA defect was not the priority ORDER — it was that ADJACENT YEARS came from DIFFERENT
223	    # tags: MA filed both `Revenues` (net) and `RevenueFromContract…` (gross) for 2018-2021, the
224	    # gross tag won by priority, and from 2022 only the net tag remained → a phantom -25.5% step at
225	    # the seam and a 5y CAGR of 6.78% instead of 16.47%. When one tag spans the whole range, using
226	    # it alone removes the question entirely; conflict resolution is only needed when none does.
227	    per_tag, tag_conflicts = {}, []
228	    for tag in tags:
229	        units = _concept(facts, taxonomy, tag)
230	        if not units:
231	            continue
232	        key = _pick_unit(units)
233	        if not key:
234	            continue
235	        this = {}
236	        for f in units[key]:
237	            if not f.get("form", "").startswith("10-K"):
238	                continue
239	            end, start = f.get("end"), f.get("start")
240	            if end is None:
241	                continue
242	            if start is not None and _days(start, end) < 300:
243	                continue
244	            filed = f.get("filed", "")
245	            if end not in this or filed > this[end]["filed"]:
246	                # v4.2.47: carry FULL provenance — a jump means nothing without knowing whether
247	                # the tag, the unit, the form or the filing changed underneath it.
248	                this[end] = {"end": end, "val": f.get("val"), "accn": f.get("accn"), "filed": filed,
249	                             "unit": key, "form": f.get("form")}
250	        if drop_zero:
251	            for end in [e for e, r in this.items() if r["val"] == 0 or r["val"] is None]:
252	                dropped.append(end)
253	                del this[end]
254	        if this:
255	            per_tag[tag] = this
256	    # conflict detection: same fiscal year reported by 2+ tags with materially different values
257	    all_ends = sorted({e for t in per_tag.values() for e in t})
258	    for end in all_ends:
259	        vals = {tag: t[end]["val"] for tag, t in per_tag.items() if end in t and t[end]["val"]}
260	        if len(vals) > 1:
261	            lo, hi = min(vals.values()), max(vals.values())
262	            if hi > 0 and (hi - lo) / hi > 0.05:
263	                tag_conflicts.append({"end": end, "values": vals, "spread_pct": round((hi - lo) / hi * 100, 1)})
264	    # MAIN RULE (v4.2.53, mandate NNN): a single tag that covers the WINDOWS ACTUALLY USED by the
265	    # growth anchor wins outright — no stitching. The previous form demanded coverage of the WHOLE
266	    # observed range and therefore never fired: MA's `Revenues` covers 18 of 19 years (2015 absent),
267	    # one hole disqualified it, the code fell back to priority stitching and the gross tag won
268	    # 2018-2021 again — the anchor stayed 6.78% instead of 13.82% through a full re-run.
269	    # Class, to protocol: THE FITNESS OF DATA IS JUDGED ON THE WINDOW OF USE, NOT ON THE WHOLE
270	    # SERIES. A gap outside every window cannot corrupt an anchor computed inside them.
271	    # Gap-filling from a second tag stays REJECTED: stitching is stitching, and a tag agreeing on
272	    # the overlap is DIAGNOSTIC of reliability, never a source of values.
273	    ANCHOR_WINDOWS = (3, 5)
274	    def _covers_windows(years):
275	        if not all_ends:
276	            return False
277	        last = max(int(e[:4]) for e in all_ends)
278	        have = {int(e[:4]) for e in years}
279	        for w in ANCHOR_WINDOWS:
280	            need = set(range(last - w, last + 1))   # w+1 points make a w-year CAGR
281	            if not need.issubset(have):
282	                return False
283	        return True
284	    full = [tag for tag in tags if tag in per_tag and _covers_windows(per_tag[tag])]
285	    if full:
286	        chosen = full[0]
287	        by_end = dict(per_tag[chosen])
288	        used.add(chosen)
289	        # gaps OUTSIDE the anchor windows are recorded, not repaired — visible, never filled
290	        _gaps = sorted(set(all_ends) - set(by_end))
291	        if _gaps:
292	            tag_conflicts.append({"note": "single-tag series chosen on window coverage; "
293	                                  "years outside the anchor windows are absent by construction",
294	                                  "absent_years": [g[:4] for g in _gaps], "chosen_tag": chosen})
295	    else:
296	        for tag in tags:
297	            for end, rec in (per_tag.get(tag) or {}).items():
298	                if end in by_end:
299	                    continue
300	                by_end[end] = rec
301	                used.add(tag)
302	    year_tag = {}
303	    for tag, t in per_tag.items():
304	        for end, rec in t.items():
305	            if by_end.get(end) is rec:
306	                year_tag[end] = tag
307	    return ([dict(by_end[k], tag=year_tag.get(k)) for k in sorted(by_end)], used,
308	            sorted(set(dropped) - set(by_end)), tag_conflicts)

312	_PROV_COSIGNAL = ("accession",)           # routine: changes on 76-89% of seams (MA/NFLX measured)

315	def _provenance_of(rec):
316	    """v4.2.48: provenance of a series point, split into PRIMARY and CO-SIGNAL fields.
317	
318	    `accession` was measured on live data: it changes on 76% of MA's year seams and 89% of NFLX's,
319	    because each year is taken from whichever 10-K covers it — recent years ride the latest report
320	    as comparatives, older years their own. That boundary is set by report COVERAGE, not by data
321	    integrity, so treating it as a defect signal on its own produces a gate that fires almost
322	    always. It is therefore a CO-SIGNAL: informative only alongside a primary change.
323	    """
324	    return {"tag": rec.get("tag"), "unit": rec.get("unit"),
325	            "form": rec.get("form"), "accession": rec.get("accn")}

328	def _ratio_continuity(num_series, den_series, tol=0.30):
329	    """v4.2.48 (mandate FFF, corrected twice on live data): a jump is a DEFECT only when it
330	    coincides with a PRIMARY provenance change; a jump whose provenance cannot be compared is
331	    neither, and says so.
332	
333	    Two live corrections shaped this. (1) Magnitude alone is not a criterion: MA's real tag switch
334	    moved the operating margin 63%, NFLX moved it 88% and 277% on a single tag — a real business
335	    out-jumps a data defect. (2) `accession` is routine (76%/89% of seams), so it was demoted to a
336	    co-signal; keeping it primary would fire on ordinary report coverage.
337	
338	    THREE outcomes, because absence of provenance is not sameness of provenance:
339	      defects            — a primary field (tag/unit/form) demonstrably CHANGED, or a fiscal year
340	                           is missing across the step;
341	      provenance_unknown — the jump exists but at least one primary field is unknown on either
342	                           side, so nothing can be compared. Honest "don't know", not silence;
343	      business_events    — provenance fully known, fully unchanged: a real step in the business.
344	
345	    Returns {"defects": [...], "provenance_unknown": [...], "business_events": [...]}.
346	    """
347	    num = {r["end"]: r["val"] for r in (num_series or []) if r.get("val")}
348	    den = {r["end"]: r for r in (den_series or []) if r.get("val")}
349	    ends = sorted(set(num) & set(den))
350	    defects, unknown, events, prev = [], [], [], None
351	    for end in ends:
352	        d = den[end]
353	        if not d["val"]:
354	            continue
355	        ratio = num[end] / d["val"]
356	        if prev is not None and prev["ratio"] > 0 and ratio > 0:
357	            jump = abs(ratio - prev["ratio"]) / prev["ratio"]
358	            if jump > tol:
359	                cur_p, prev_p = _provenance_of(d), prev["prov"]
360	                changed, uncomparable = [], []
361	                for f in _PROV_PRIMARY:
362	                    a, b = prev_p.get(f), cur_p.get(f)
363	                    if a is None or b is None:
364	                        uncomparable.append(f)
365	                    elif a != b:
366	                        changed.append(f)
367	                co = [f for f in _PROV_COSIGNAL
368	                      if prev_p.get(f) is not None and cur_p.get(f) is not None
369	                      and prev_p.get(f) != cur_p.get(f)]
370	                try:
371	                    gap = int(end[:4]) - int(prev["end"][:4]) > 1
372	                except Exception:
373	                    gap = False
374	                if gap:
375	                    changed.append("year_gap")
376	                rec = {"end": end, "prev_end": prev["end"],
377	                       "ratio": round(ratio, 4), "prev_ratio": round(prev["ratio"], 4),
378	                       "jump_pct": round(jump * 100, 1),
379	                       "tag": d.get("tag"), "prev_tag": prev_p.get("tag"),
380	                       "provenance_changed": changed,
381	                       "provenance_uncomparable": uncomparable,
382	                       "cosignal_changed": co}
383	                if changed:
384	                    defects.append(rec)
385	                elif uncomparable:
386	                    unknown.append(rec)
387	                else:
388	                    events.append(rec)
389	        prev = {"end": end, "ratio": ratio, "prov": _provenance_of(d)}
390	    return {"defects": defects, "provenance_unknown": unknown, "business_events": events}

393	def _flag_stale(series):
394	    """Flag years whose val EXACTLY equals another year's AND differs from a neighbor by >=3x."""
395	    vals = [(p["end"], p["val"]) for p in series if p.get("val") not in (None, 0)]
396	    n = len(vals)
397	    suspects = []
398	    for i, (end, v) in enumerate(vals):
399	        if not any(j != i and vals[j][1] == v for j in range(n)):
400	            continue
401	        neigh = []
402	        if i > 0:
403	            neigh.append(vals[i - 1][1])
404	        if i < n - 1:
405	            neigh.append(vals[i + 1][1])
406	        av = abs(v)
407	        big = any(av and x and (max(av, abs(x)) / max(min(av, abs(x)), 1) >= 3) for x in neigh)
408	        if big:
409	            suspects.append(end)
410	    return suspects

416	def _detect_confirmed_splits(facts, tags, taxonomy="us-gaap", cik=None):
417	    """Scan ALL filings (not deduped-to-latest) for a fiscal year-end reported with two
418	    MATERIALLY DIFFERENT values across different accessions -- i.e. a later filing retroactively
419	    restated an earlier year's share count. This only happens for genuine stock splits (never for
420	    organic dilution, which is never restated). Returns [{end, factor, earliest_val, earliest_filed,
421	    latest_val, latest_filed, tag}] -- positive, SEC-sourced confirmation, not a heuristic guess.
422	
423	    PER-TAG, deliberately (v4.2.3). A restatement is within-tag evidence: the same tag, the same
424	    period, two values. Until v4.2.3 all tags pooled into one bucket per end-date, so for a company
425	    reporting BOTH basic and diluted weighted averages (live NFLX does; every fixture used one tag)
426	    lo = basic pre-split and hi = diluted post-split, and the ratio absorbed the basic/diluted
427	    dilution wedge: a clean 10.00x read as ~10.17x, missing the 1% tolerance. The split stayed
428	    unconfirmed on live data while the suite was green -- deterministically, on every run."""
429	    confirmed_by_end = {}
430	    for tag in tags:
431	        units = _concept(facts, taxonomy, tag)
432	        # companyfacts alone is not sufficient -- see _merge_units. Ask companyconcept for the
433	        # same tag and union the two; the restatement lives in whichever one kept it.
434	        if cik:
435	            try:
436	                units = _merge_units(units, _companyconcept(cik, taxonomy, tag))
437	            except Exception:
438	                pass
439	        if not units:
440	            continue
441	        key = _pick_unit(units)
442	        if not key:
443	            continue
444	        by_end = {}  # THIS tag only -- never pool values across tags (see docstring)
445	        for f in units[key]:
446	            if not f.get("form", "").startswith("10-K"):
447	                continue
448	            end, start, val, filed = f.get("end"), f.get("start"), f.get("val"), f.get("filed", "")
449	            if end is None or val is None:
450	                continue
451	            if start is not None and _days(start, end) < 300:
452	                continue
453	            by_end.setdefault(end, []).append({"val": val, "filed": filed, "accn": f.get("accn")})
454	        for end, rows in by_end.items():
455	            if end in confirmed_by_end:
456	                continue  # tags are priority-ordered; the first tag to confirm an end wins
457	            distinct_vals = sorted(set(r["val"] for r in rows if r["val"]))
458	            if len(distinct_vals) < 2:
459	                continue
460	            lo, hi = distinct_vals[0], distinct_vals[-1]
461	            if lo <= 0:
462	                continue
463	            ratio = hi / lo
464	            factor = next((c for c in _CLEAN_SPLIT_FACTORS if abs(ratio - c) / c <= 0.01), None)
465	            if not factor:
466	                continue
467	            earliest = min([r for r in rows if r["val"] == lo], key=lambda r: r["filed"])
468	            latest = max([r for r in rows if r["val"] == hi], key=lambda r: r["filed"])
469	            # require the restatement to be genuinely LATER (positive confirmation, not filing-order noise)
470	            if latest["filed"] > earliest["filed"]:
471	                confirmed_by_end[end] = {"end": end, "factor": factor,
472	                                         "earliest_val": earliest["val"], "earliest_filed": earliest["filed"],
473	                                         "latest_val": latest["val"], "latest_filed": latest["filed"],
474	                                         "tag": tag}
475	    return sorted(confirmed_by_end.values(), key=lambda c: c["end"])

709	    # v4.2.32 mandate (b): DEBT RECONCILIATION GATE. Not a third patch on tag priority — a gate.
710	    # MA 2026-07-22: the LongTermDebt tag returned $21M while the assembled components said $19.0B
711	    # (a 99.9% divergence). The chosen figure went straight into D/E = 0.0027 and the GPS D-block

722	    _comp_sum = None
723	    # v4.2.33 mandate (1): expose the ACTUAL tags behind every component, so a reader can audit the

746	                "(possible double count across tags)" % (_comp_sum, _chosen, DOUBLE_COUNT_X))
747	        if _rel > RECON_TOL and _comp_sum > _chosen:
748	            # (1) components win when they diverge >20% AND read HIGHER. The "higher wins" rule is
749	            # the same conservatism the mandate sets in (2), and it is required for correctness:
750	            # DEBT_FULL_LT already INCLUDES current maturities, so a components sum that is SMALLER
751	            # is simply the noncurrent part (NFLX: full 21.86B vs noncurrent-only 11.83B) and must
752	            # NOT displace the fuller figure — that was the v4.2.23 defect. A components sum that is

754	            out["total_debt"] = _comp_sum

759	            out["_flags"]["debt_uncertain"] = (
760	                "tag and components disagree by %.1f%% — leverage reading disputed" % (_rel * 100))
761	            src["total_debt"] = "components_sum(reconciled)"
762	        elif _rel > RECON_TOL:
763	            # divergence exists but the chosen (fuller) figure reads higher — keep it, still flag.
764	            out["_flags"]["total_debt_divergence"] = True
765	    elif isinstance(_chosen, (int, float)) and _chosen > 0:

768	        for _tags in (DEBT_FULL_LT, DEBT_COMBINED):
769	            _v, _t = _latest_instant(facts, _tags)

773	            _mx, _mx_tag = max(_alts, key=lambda x: x[0])
774	            if _mx > 0 and abs(_mx - _chosen) / max(_mx, _chosen) > RECON_TOL:
775	                out["total_debt"] = _mx           # conservative = larger
776	                out["_flags"]["debt_uncertain"] = (
777	                    "sources diverge >%.0f%%: chose conservative %.0f (%s) over %.0f"
778	                    % (RECON_TOL * 100, _mx, _mx_tag, _chosen))
779	                out["_flags"]["total_debt_divergence"] = True
780	                src["total_debt"] = _mx_tag
781

786	    conf_splits = _detect_confirmed_splits(facts, DURATION_TAGS["shares_diluted"], cik=cik)
787	    if conf_splits:

789	    else:

792	        out["_flags"]["confirmed_splits_none"] = (
793	            "no retroactive share-count restatement found in companyfacts+companyconcept "
794	            "10-K history; a clean ratio jump downstream is UNCONFIRMED, not proven dilution")
795	
796	    # v4.2.60: publish dps_series ONLY when it can be trusted. Per-share amounts are as-reported,
797	    # so a stock split inside the window makes pre-split DPS incomparable with post-split DPS and
798	    # the CAGR becomes a split artifact wearing a dividend's name — the exact defect that cost the
799	    # NVDA/shares work in v4.2.2. There is no split-normalisation for DPS in this codebase yet, so

819	
820	    out["_field_sources"] = src
